title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
authors: Lingxian Kong, Yuta Murakami, Ryuichi Shindou, Zhiyuan Sun
abstract: arXiv:2610.28760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.
summary:
- Low bias: static state with parallel valley pseudospins; high bias: layer‑spin precession locks valleys antiparallel.
- Dynamical tunneling blockade suppresses interlayer tunneling, eliminating ac current and sharply reducing dc current.
- Contrasts with conventional quantum Hall double layers, revealing a new nonequilibrium regime in flat‑band systems.

title: Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
abstract: arXiv:2610.28786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological $p_x+ip_y$ pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by integrating out the hole degrees of freedom reproduces these results and shows how pairing may endow electrons with effective Berry curvature. Finally, through symmetry analysis, we show that intrinsic resonances near the superconducting gap edge are allowed in nonunitary states but forbidden in unitary states. Our work thus establishes quantum geometry as a unifying principle for the intrinsic Hall response in superconductors and provides a guide for distinguishing different candidate TRSB pairings.
summary:
- Unified theory of intrinsic optical Hall effect in TRSB multiband superconductors, linking the response to quantum‑geometric interband velocity (Berry connection).
- Distinguishes unitary vs nonunitary TRSB states: interband pairing is required for unitary Hall response, while nonunitary states can exhibit Hall via single‑electron tunneling if spin‑orbit coupling is present.
- Identifies two tunneling channels—single‑electron and Cooper‑pair—driven by interband processes, and derives an effective theory by integrating out hole degrees of freedom.

title: Polymer-Mediated Hotspot Evolution in Shock-Induced Pore Collapse in 1,3,5,7-Tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocane (HMX)-based Explosives
authors: Jalen Macatangay, Brenden W. Hamilton, Alejandro Strachan
abstract: arXiv:2610.28812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The initiation of detonation in high explosives (HEs) under shock loading is strongly influenced by the collapse of porosity and the subsequent formation of hotspots. As these materials are widely integrated with polymer binders to form polymer-bonded explosives, the collapse of pores at explosive-binder interfaces has received significant interest. Recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the shock-driven expansion of soft polymers (e.g. polystyrene) into a void produces greater pressure-volume (PV) work during recompression and higher local temperatures compared to pore collapse in neat HEs, ultimately expediting the onset of chemical reactions. Yet how pore collapse, interfacial phenomena, and binder chemistry jointly affect initiation remains insufficiently understood. We provide deeper insights into the role of polymer in hotspot evolution through reactive MD simulations, specifically characterizing its chemical behavior during the shock-induced collapse of voids at sizes approaching experimentally relevant length scales. We consider the HE 1,3,5,7-Tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocane (HMX) in a crystal-gap-crystal stack with polystyrene along the upstream surface. In the hydrodynamic collapse regime, hotspots nucleate at the material interfaces, with void length-dependence in PV work, shock temperature, and the onset of self-sustaining chemistry. Driven by shock-induced deformation and HMX decomposition, the binder undergoes backbone chain scission followed by extensive aromatic-backbone cross-bonding, akin to a graphite to diamond transformation. These reactions act as heat sinks, suppressing deflagration and ultimately inhibiting hotspot growth and coalescence between crystals. The simulations further link the polymer's chemical response to the shock-to-detonation transition in polymer-bonded explosives.
summary:
- Polystyrene expansion into voids during shock collapse boosts PV work and hotspot temperatures, accelerating HMX decomposition.
- Hotspots nucleate at polymer–HMX interfaces; void size governs PV work, shock temperature, and reaction onset.
- Reactive MD shows binder chemistry and interfacial deformation jointly dictate self‑sustaining detonation initiation.

title: Paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$: complete one phonon Raman spectrum
authors: Taras Palasyuk, Dominik Kurzyd{\l}owski, Ashutosh S. Wadge, Rajmund Bacewicz, Madhavi H. Dalsaniya, Micha{\l} Wierzbicki, Daniel Jastrzebski, Andrzej Wi\'sniewski, Wojciech Szuszkiewicz, Igor Antoniazzi, Bruno Camargo, Maciej R. Molas, Adam Babi\'nski, Krzysztof Zberecki, Cezariusz Jastrzebski
abstract: arXiv:2610.28844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study we present a complete first-order Raman scattering spectrum of paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$- a material, where new type of spin texture induced by noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the N\'eel temperature ($T_N \approx 90$ K) gives rise to unconventional scenario of magnetism. Basic properties of all five phonon modes ($A_g$, $E_g$ and three $T_g$) predicted by the group theory have been successfully approached through polarization, excitation and temperature dependent measurements. In particular, the ever-missing phonon mode of $T_g$ symmetry has been unambiguously resolved in the room temperature Raman spectrum at approximately 107 cm$^{-1}$, just 1.5 cm$^{-1}$ higher in frequency compared to the $E_g$ mode. Density functional theory calculations reproduce the observed Raman-active phonon spectrum and support the assignment of all five first-order Raman modes, including the near-degeneracy of the $E_g$ and one of the $T_g$ vibrations. The calculations further reveal a dense manifold of low-energy antiferromagnetic spin configurations, separated from the ground state by only a few meV per formula unit. Furthermore, strong signals of inelastically scattered light from the paramagnetic (PM) phase of MnTe$_2$ were acquired with long wavelength excitations, i.e. 633 nm and 785 nm, revealing the $2A_g$ overtone at approx. 360 cm$^{-1}$. The enhanced absorption of the light in the near infrared range could be a putative reason behind the anomalous angular dependence of scattered intensity of the highest frequency $T_g$ phonon mode (183 cm$^{-1}$) measured in PM MnTe$_2$ with parallelly aligned polarizers. Finally, upon cooling just below the $T_N$, the measured properties of phonons remained basically unperturbed by the incipient long-range antiferromagnetic ordering.
summary:
- First‑order Raman spectrum of paramagnetic MnTe₂ fully resolved, revealing all five phonon modes (Ag, Eg, three Tg) and the previously missing Tg mode at ~107 cm⁻¹.
- DFT reproduces the spectrum, confirms Eg–Tg near‑degeneracy, and uncovers a dense manifold of low‑energy antiferromagnetic spin states within a few meV of the ground state.
- Long‑wavelength (633/785 nm) excitation yields strong inelastic scattering, detecting a 2Ag overtone near 360 cm⁻¹ and indicating enhanced near‑IR absorption

title: Two quantum skyrmions form a magnon Josephson junction
abstract: arXiv:2610.28854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two quantum skyrmions in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ magnet bind into a molecule, and the molecule acts as a magnon Josephson junction: the relative helicity $\theta$ and the number $n$ of magnons transferred between them obey $H=E_Cn^2-W\cos\theta$. DMRG on the $J_1$--$J_2$ triangular lattice gives $E_C$ as the curvature of the skyrmion energy at its natural size of seven flipped spins, and the measured helicity coherence fixes $W\simeq0.02J_1$, half the skyrmion--antiskyrmion tunnel splitting and independent of the anisotropy. Two helicity qubits side by side are thus strongly coupled by their own interaction.
summary:
- Two quantum skyrmions bind into a molecule that behaves as a magnon Josephson junction, \(H=E_C n^2-W\cos\theta\).
- DMRG on the \(J_1\)–\(J_2\) triangular lattice gives \(E_C\) from the energy curvature at seven flipped spins and \(W\simeq02J_1\), half the skyrmion–antiskyrmion tunneling splitting, independent of anisotropy.
- The helicity qubits on either side are strongly coupled through this intrinsic interaction, offering a new qubit architecture.

title: Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy of Ce and U Oxides
abstract: arXiv:2610.28857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The soft x-ray Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy (RIPES) of the M5 transition in cerium oxide and the N5 transition in uranium dioxide and supporting instrumentation is discussed. Further experimental evidence and analysis is presented to support the hypothesis that the Ce 5d states are intrinsic to the resonance process in cerium oxide. The strong connection with cerium dioxide is emphasized.
summary:
- Soft‑X‑ray RIPES examines M5 (Ce) and N5 (U) transitions in CeO₂ and UO₂.
- Data confirm Ce 5d states are intrinsic to the resonance process in CeO₂.
- Highlights a strong link between resonance features and cerium dioxide’s electronic structure.

title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
authors: Salman Ahsanullah, Neema Rafizadeh, Hui Zhao
abstract: arXiv:2610.28877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI$_2$ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic exciton transport and highlight the critical role of interface protection in air-sensitive van der Waals materials.
summary:
- Ultrafast, highly anisotropic exciton diffusion in NbOI₂, with D≈160 cm² s⁻¹ along the nonpolar axis, ~2× higher than the polar direction.
- Diffusion anisotropy reflects the low‑symmetry crystal structure and ranks among the highest for van der Waals semiconductors.
- Fabrication and encapsulation protocols that ensure long‑term environmental stability are identified, highlighting the need for interface protection.

title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
authors: Yasir Mahmood, Daniel Wines, Viviana Dovale-Farelo, Kamal Choudhary, Lucas M Hale
abstract: arXiv:2610.28967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon nanowires (Si NWs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation nanoelectronic devices due to their tunable electronic properties, and compatibility with aggressive scaling requirements. The integration of strain further enhances their performance by modulating carrier mobility, band structure, and transport behavior without altering material chemistry. Within the NW, the silicon-silicon dioxide (Si-SiO$_{2}$) interface serves as a critical region where strain redistribution and suboxide bonding collectively influence the mechanical and electronic response. Here, we combine reactive force field molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations to investigate how oxidation-induced interfacial structure and crystallographic facet orientation govern strain-dependent bond evolution and facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties in oxidized Si NWs. Simulated dry thermal oxidation generates chemically realistic Si-SiO$_{2}$ interfaces, enabling direct characterization of bond order redistribution and stress gradient development across the interface under tensile strain. Interfacial Si-Si bonds exhibit elongation and reduced bond order associated with partial oxidation states, leading to localized stress concentration and preferential bond rupture. Complementary density functional theory calculations on facet-specific models reveal that orientation-dependent interfacial bonding modulates facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties. Together, these results establish a direct coupling between interfacial suboxide chemistry, mechanical deformation, and electronic structure, providing atomistic insight into strain-modulated behavior at oxidized silicon interfaces in faceted NWs.
summary:
- Strain concentrates at the Si‑SiO₂ interface, elongating Si–Si bonds and triggering localized rupture.
- Oxidation state and crystallographic facet orientation jointly dictate how electronic properties shift under strain.
- Reactive MD plus DFT reveal facet‑dependent strain responses in oxidized silicon nanowires.

title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction
authors: Justin Tahmassebpur, Chia-Hao Lee, Cristob\'al M\'endez, Shake Karapetyan, Schuyler Z. Shi, David A. Muller, Tom\'as Arias
abstract: arXiv:2610.28996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard genetic algorithms. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory into a genetic algorithm to enable efficient global search through a differentiable effective-atom representation. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ containing 1150 atoms from ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.
summary:
- Introduces Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), a genetic algorithm with differentiable effective‑atom representation for large‑scale structure prediction.
- Uses a crossover that superimposes parent structures and relaxes the result, enabling efficient global search.
- Outperforms baselines on 240‑atom H sublattice recovery, 364‑atom edge‑dislocation core prediction, and 1150‑atom twisted‑bilayer WSe₂ reconstruction.

title: Influence of embedding depth on the pullout of a plate from a confined granular medium
authors: Dominik Krengel, Jian Chen, Shun Nomura, Hidenori Takahashi
abstract: arXiv:2610.29016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. We find that the peak and steady-state drag forces depend differently on their embedding depth for different friction coefficients. Depending on the strength of friction the plate may interact with the domain walls, which enhances the drag force until failure of the aggregate, but not in the steady-state as dilation around intruder directs the force chains emanating from the plate upwards and away from the walls. If the inter-particle friction is weak, it is possible for the overhead pressure to overcome frictional resistance beyond a certain embedding depth. This prevents the formation of dilated failure zones above the intruder and changes the failure mode of the aggregate, leading to a slower decay of the steady-state drag forces with pullout distance.
summary:
- Peak and steady‑state drag of a pulled plate depend on depth and inter‑particle friction.
- High friction lets wall forces boost drag until failure; steady state redirects chains upward, reducing wall effects.
- Low friction lets overburden pressure dominate at deep depths, suppressing dilation and slowing the decay of steady‑state drag.

title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
authors: Masoud Mardani, Shivani Sharma, Saul H. Lapidus, Theo Siegrist
abstract: arXiv:2610.29180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.
summary:
- EuPd₂Si₂ undergoes a valence transition at 143 K; Ge substitution lowers Tv (87 K at x = and alters lattice constants.
- Synchrotron X‑ray diffraction shows Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ phase coexistence across Tv, with peak broadening indicating strain‑stabilized segregation.
- The gradual transition couples structural strain to electronic valence, yielding an inverse linear Tv–lattice‑parameter relationship.

title: Interplay of disorder and phonons in two-dimensional transport
abstract: arXiv:2610.29260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the temperature- and density-dependent resistivity of bilayer MoSe$_2$ in the presence of charged impurities, short-range defects, and longitudinal acoustic phonons, using the Boltzmann transport theory with screening treated in the random phase approximation, and compare the results with recent transport measurements. The disorder parameters are taken from the experiment itself and the phonon parameters are taken from literature estimates for MoSe$_2$. We find that screened acoustic phonons are a small correction to the disorder-limited resistivity over the entire experimental temperature range, so that the temperature dependence of the measured resistivity on the metallic side is controlled by the temperature-dependent screening of charged disorder and by neutral defects. We also show that a resistivity minimum as a function of temperature can arise on both sides of the metal-insulator crossover through two different mechanisms: on the insulating side from the interplay between activated carriers and resistive scattering, and on the metallic side from the interplay between disorder and phonon scattering. The existence of a resistivity minimum by itself therefore does not identify the phase.
summary:
- Bilayer MoSe₂ resistivity is governed mainly by screened charged impurities and neutral defects; acoustic phonons give only a minor correction.
- A resistivity minimum appears on both metallic and insulating sides: on the insulating side from activated carriers, on the metallic side from disorder–phonon interplay.
- Boltzmann transport with RPA screening reproduces experimental temperature‑ and density‑dependent data, confirming phonons are negligible over the measured range.

title: Ab Initio Approach for Quantum Magnets with Coupled Cluster and Transcorrelation
authors: Kristoffer Simula, Nikolay A. Bogdanov, Olle Gunnarsson, Daniel Kats, Ali Alavi
abstract: arXiv:2610.29324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nearest-neighbour exchange coupling $J_1$ is the simplest ingredient of model Hamiltonians used to understand magnetism in real materials. Nevertheless, its ab initio determination requires a high-level correlation treatment and a large basis for wave function expansion. Here we compute $J_1$ for five oxygen-bridged spin-1/2 quantum magnets --- Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, La$_2$CuO$_4$, NdNiO$_2$, ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$, and Li$_2$CuO$_2$ --- spanning bridging angles from 180$^\circ$ to 94$^\circ$ and the crossover from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic coupling, using embedded-cluster methodology. To describe the open-shell singlets we use 2-determinant coupled cluster with single and double excitations, which recovers the orbital-breathing enhancement of superexchange from a minimal reference. Basis-set errors are found to be large: extrapolation to the complete basis-set (CBS) limit shifts $J_1$ by up to 50 meV from bases of double-$\zeta$ quality. Transcorrelated Hamiltonians reproduce the CBS estimates with modest basis set sizes, yielding an excellent accuracy against experiment at highly affordable cost. These results are the first application of transcorrelated methods in strongly correlated solid-state systems, and establish transcorrelation as a powerful theory in computational research of materials.
summary:
- Ab initio determination of nearest‑neighbour exchange \(J_1\) in five oxygen‑bridged spin‑½ quantum magnets using embedded‑cluster 2‑determinant CCSD.
- Basis‑set errors are large; CBS extrapolation shifts \(J_1\) by up to 50 meV, while transcorrelated Hamiltonians recover CBS accuracy with modest basis sizes.
- First demonstration of transcorrelated methods in strongly correlated solids, showing high accuracy and affordable cost for magnetic coupling predictions.

title: Quantics tensor trains for multiloop functional renormalization group in multiorbital impurity models
abstract: arXiv:2610.29341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The full frequency dependence of electronic interactions is central to dynamical correlations, but its numerical cost restricts multiorbital calculations. We formulate the multiloop functional renormalization group directly in the quantics tensor train representation, retaining all three independent vertex frequencies over broad ranges without an explicit high-frequency parametrization. Analytical tensor operators perform frequency transformations and internal summations without dense vertex intermediates. Multiloop corrections improve agreement of vertices and responses with independent references and reproduce the low-energy numerical renormalization group self-energy. Lower-temperature calculations resolve a quadratic frequency contribution to the analytically continued scattering rate. A degenerate two-orbital impurity exhibits distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses at fixed Hund coupling. In a compensated altermagnetic environment, an orbital-level splitting induces a local spin response despite zero magnetization of the unperturbed impurity. Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.
summary:
- Multiloop functional renormalization group reformulated in quantics tensor‑train representation, handling full three‑frequency vertex dependence without explicit high‑frequency parametrization.
- Achieves quantitative agreement with reference methods and reproduces low‑energy NRG self‑energy; uncovers a quadratic frequency term in the scattering rate at low temperatures.
- Reveals distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses in a two‑orbital impurity under Hund coupling and altermagnetic conditions, with Hund coupling suppressing orbital response while enhancing spin polarization.

title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying, Mingquan He
abstract: arXiv:2610.29366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.
summary:
- Hybridization of flat kagome bands with dispersive bands in CsCr₆Sb₆ creates a Kondo‑like heavy‑fermion state, boosting Seebeck and Nernst coefficients below ~70 K.
- The Nernst coefficient follows universal heavy‑fermion scaling (30–80 K), signaling strongly renormalized quasiparticles and short‑range antiferromagnetic correlations.
- Maxima in Seebeck and Nernst signals near 20–25 K indicate combined

title: Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe2
authors: Abdurrafi Ahsan Alghifari, Euihwan Do, Jae Whan Park, Han Woong Yeom
abstract: arXiv:2610.29448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.
summary:
- Ab initio calculations reveal a chiral monoclinic (CCDW in 1T‑TiSe₂ stabilized by cooperative phonon condensation, reproducing the observed energy gap and topography.
- The potential is exceptionally soft along the symmetry‑breaking direction, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while preserving an average chiral structure.
- This dynamical chiral CDW reconciles chiral domains seen in imaging with symmetry loss in bulk spectroscopy, highlighting lattice instability and fluctuations as the microscopic origin of chirality.

title: On thermal Hall effect in boson systems
authors: Yu. V. Baramygina, D. N. Aristov
abstract: arXiv:2610.29482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically discuss the thermal Hall effect (THE) in boson systems keeping in mind possible applications to magnetically ordered insulators with skyrmion lattice ground state. The magnon spectrum of such systems may undergo a topological transition upon the variation of magnetic field, and THE could be a tool to confirm this phenomenon. We rederive formulas, suitable for our purposes, and find expressions which have a different temperature dependence of THE as compared to previously reported results. Particularly, in presence of anomalous terms in magnon Hamiltonian the thermal Hall conductivity has a small but finite residual 1/T contribution. Such contribution may become sizable at very low temperatures and resembles Meissner effect in superconducting metals.
summary:
- Investigates thermal Hall effect (THE) in bosonic magnon systems, especially skyrmion lattice insulators.
- Derives new temperature‑dependent formulas, revealing a finite 1/T residual term when anomalous magnon interactions are present.
- Suggests THE can detect topological transitions in magnon spectra and may mimic a Meissner‑like effect at low temperatures.

title: Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ by broad range $^{139}$La-NQR
authors: Tillmann Weinhold, Jerin Abraham George, Cornelius Herrmann, Domenic Nowak, Rajib Sarkar, Felix Seewald, Rowena Wachtel, Sabine Wurmehl, Bernd B\"uchner, Hans-Henning Klauss
summary:
- 139La‑NQR confirms non‑collinear spin‑ice antiferromagnetic order in La₂O₂Fe₂OSe₂ below ~90 K.
- νQ, 2νQ, and 3νQ resonances agree with prior NMR/Mössbauer data, validating the magnetic structure.
- No substantial change in the La electric‑field gradient is observed below TN, contradicting earlier claims.
